Creativity Techniques · U4 Applying Creativity Techniques in the Workplace

1 · Generate before you judge

An unrelated picture can open a route through a workplace brief. The deadline can stay fixed.

Give each group member a folder containing two or three pictures that are not related to the problem area.

(Michalko 2010, 440)

Image: Overhead view of workshop tables with groups in an education session.

Groups participating in the Wikipedia for Education workshop 01 · Mounir Neddi · CC0 1.0 · Source

  • The first lesson protects a generation window inside a real brief.
  • Ask a Crab uses unrelated pictures as prompts; the class adapts its five-step blueprint.
  • The timer is a professor proposal, not a source instruction.

Source: (Michalko 2010, 440).

Ask: What can the image open that the first reading of the brief did not?

Creativity Techniques · U4 Applying Creativity Techniques in the Workplace

2 · Build on the connection

Read ideas aloud, add a modification, and record the new route before evaluation.

As each idea is read, ask the group members to discuss it and try to develop new ideas or modifications.

(Michalko 2010, 440)

Image: Historic plate showing drafting-room layout and method diagrams from 1918.

Drafting room methods (1918) (14591687900) · Charles Dickey Collins · Public domain · Source

  • Let the group develop or modify ideas before it evaluates.
  • Save who added each change so the contribution trail does not disappear.

Source: (Michalko 2010, 440).

Ask: Which addition changed the direction of the first idea?

Creativity Techniques · U4 Applying Creativity Techniques in the Workplace

3 · Follow the route from another point of view

Observe where a first-time visitor looks, pauses, turns, or asks what to do next.

People turn around to find out what it's really like to be someone in a different position.

(Michalko 2010, 371)

Image: Black-and-white photograph of a large drafting room with rows of tables.

Drafting room, Navy Dept. LCCN2016873947 · Harris & Ewing · Public domain · Source

  • U4.2 starts from the idea set saved in U4.1, then observes a route rather than running another vote.
  • Record what a walker does and says before interpreting it.
  • The classroom route walk is a course adaptation, not representative visitor research.

Source: (Michalko 2010, 371).

Ask: What would a real visitor need to tell you that this walkthrough cannot?

Creativity Techniques · U4 Applying Creativity Techniques in the Workplace

4 · Record what happened before you explain it

Use observations to choose an idea for the next check; one peer walkthrough cannot speak for every visitor.

Recording particular behavior, words, and actions that critically affected their attitude as 'buyers.'

(Michalko 2010, 371)

Image: Engraved view of designers at tables in the Navy Department designing room, 1893.

Designing room in the Navy Department, 1893 - A. Castaigne. LCCN2003662986 · J. André Castaigne · Public domain · Source

  • Separate recorded actions and words from interpretations.
  • Compare the route notes with U4.1's saved idea set and carry forward one idea that responds to an observed moment.
  • The role rotation, selection criterion, and next-check question are course adaptations. A peer walkthrough is not representative visitor research.

Source: (Michalko 2010, 371).

Ask: Whose experience still needs to be checked?

Creativity Techniques · U4 Applying Creativity Techniques in the Workplace

Recall check

Alone, from memory, 3 minutes. Then compare with a partner.

  1. What kind of stimulus does Ask a Crab use?
  2. Before evaluation, what does the team do with each idea?
  3. What should an observer record during a customer walkthrough?
  4. After the customer walkthrough, what do the salespeople do?
  5. What can experiencing a customer's process reveal?

Course geometric background · threshold · #7a624a21 · Original course SVG

  • Timer: 3 minutes. Students answer alone, from memory; then compare with a partner.
  • Practice only. The knowledge-test bank is a draft and is not approved for graded use.

Answers:

  • 1. Pictures unrelated to the problem area (Michalko 2010, 440).
  • 2. Discuss it, develop new ideas or modifications, and record them (Michalko 2010, 440).
  • 3. Behaviors, words, and actions that affect the customer's attitude (Michalko 2010, 371).
  • 4. Share their experiences and discuss ways to improve their own service (Michalko 2010, 371).
  • 5. What talking about another person's position alone cannot (Michalko 2010, 371).

Ask: Which answer needs another look before Lab?

Creativity Techniques · U4 Applying Creativity Techniques in the Workplace

Exercise 1 · Ask a Crab — picture diverge

Use unrelated pictures to open routes through the brief. Record the ideas and stop before evaluation.

After a designated period, ask the group members to read their ideas aloud.

(Michalko 2010, 440)

Save the brief, pictures, initial connections, additions, and note that selection was deferred.

Image: Book illustration of Ishmael and Queequeg being directed toward the Pequod.

Moby Dick p91 illustration · Augustus Burnham Shute · Public domain · Source

  • Follow the five-step Ask a Crab blueprint as a classroom adaptation: state the brief and brainstorm; distribute unrelated pictures; write and share associations; develop and record additions; defer collecting and evaluation to the next exercise.
  • The proposed twenty-minute class timing is the professor's adaptation.
  • Accessibility: students may write or type instead of speaking.

Source: (Michalko 2010, 439–440).

Ask: What did the visual prompt make possible to notice?

Creativity Techniques · U4 Applying Creativity Techniques in the Workplace

Exercise 2 · Visitor Journey Walkthrough — follow and record the route

Walk a public route from a first-time visitor's point of view. Record what happens, then choose an idea for a real check.

Recording particular behavior, words, and actions that critically affected their attitude as 'buyers.'

(Michalko 2010, 371)

Save the route and visitor task, role names, observation notes, selected U4.1 idea and criterion, and one unresolved question.

Image: Finnish road warning sign 151 depicting pedestrians.

Finland road sign 151 (1969-198?) · Arkke · Public domain · Source

  • Continue from Exercise 1; do not generate or vote on a replacement set.
  • The source describes customers' process walkthroughs and recording the behaviors, words, and actions that affect their attitude.
  • The campus route task, role rotation, observation note sheet, selection criterion, and portfolio fields are professor adaptations. Do not impersonate a disability or present peer observations as visitor research.

Source: (Michalko 2010, 371).

Ask: Which observed moment does the selected idea answer, and whose experience still needs checking?
